claude.rationale: The structural summary states the transaction is a whole-company, all-cash reverse merger in which the Company survives intact as a wholly owned subsidiary under its pre-existing name, with its customer-facing retail business, operating segment, and workforce "crossing together as a going concern rather than being carved into separate product/process/people components." Because the product (T4), operating processes (T5), and organization/people (T6) all transferred together within the surviving entity, there is no documented product-vs-process mismatch (gap_45=0) and no process-vs-people mismatch (gap_56=0). T1 is coded imprint-share because the acquirer took control while the Company's CEO was publicly stated to remain and the surviving corporation continues under its own name; no transitional-services or shared-services agreement was identified, but none was needed since no gap exists (gap_mitigated=NA).

grok.rationale: The structural summary states the deal is a whole-company reverse merger in which 'the customer-facing retail business, operating segment, and workforce ... crossing together as a going concern rather than being carved into separate product/process/people components,' so T4 and T5 moved together (gap_45=0) and T5 and T6 moved together (gap_56=0). CEO continuity and executive-retention/non-compete arrangements are noted as the principal bridges, with no TSA identified; no product-vs-process or process-vs-organization structural mismatch is documented at closing.
